newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Warsaw bourse hits high among East Europe markets.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse hits high among East Europe markets.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange led mixed trading on East European markets this week, surging to a 30-month high before retreating on a round of profit-taking.
Shares in Zagreb also hit new highs, while the Budapest, Romanian and Ljubljana bourses edged up slightly and Prague and Bratislava lost ground. Bulgarian markets held steady.
WARSAW
The Warsaw Stock Exchange soared this week, setting a 30-month high before falling on Thursday in a profit-taking correction likely to last several sessions, analysts said.
The WIG index hit 14.832.7 earlier in the week before closing on Thursday at 14,536.9, up 1.7 percent from last Friday's close.

"Prices of several stocks have risen very high so taking profits is a natural reaction and I believe there are no fundamental reasons for the fall," said Michal Szczurek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.
Analysts said the WIG index should find strong support at around 14,300 or 14,000 points, and that the market would likely rebound after the profit-taking.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest bourse edged up in flat trading this week, as investors waited on the sidelines to see if the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise interest rates next week.
The BUX index closed on Thursday at 3,539.46 points, up 6.37 from Monday's open.
"The wait-and-see attitude of the market has remained unchanged. Since news of a potential rate hike in the U.S. was released, the market has been stagnant," Peter Lencs of MKB Securities said.

Recent macroeconomic data failed to have a major impact on trading while corporate results slowed to a trickle, although plastics company Pannonplast announced a capital increase at three of its units.
PRAGUE

Czech shares lost ground over the week after the central bank placed the country's fifth largest bank, Agrobanka, under temporary forced administration due to liquidity problems, leaving some investors jittery.
The PX50 index closed Thursday's session at 568.8, off five points for the week.
Savings bank Ceska Sporitelna was indicative of the market's mood, showing heavy volatility, hitting a year high and then falling sharply.
Sporitelna particularly has been the subject of uncertainty because of the relatively large stake in the bank held by investment firm Motoinvest which was also heavily involved with Agrobanka.

"There are lots of rumours around the market with Motoinvest and no body could really tell you what the real situation is," said Robert Sekete a trader at brokerage Wood & Company. Agrobanka shares fell about 20 percent from Monday to close at 91.67 crowns on Thursday.
BRATISLAVA
Slovak blue chip shares saw a week of listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange, with further financial issues continuing to show weakness.
The 12-share SAX index held steady for the most part, closing on Thursday at 208.34 points, down slightly from Monday's open of 208.65.

Analysts said they expected lower volumes of traded stocks to result in a further decline in prices in general. "We don't expect any stronger impulse leading to a significant revival of activity on the market," said Libor Chrast of ING Barings.
BULGARIA

No corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week, as brokers and investors focused on other investments. The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) closed at 41.14 points, unchanged from last Thursday.
"Investors are shying away from the stock market and focusing their attention on government securities and foreign currency, which are more liquid and offer higher yields," one broker said.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks forged ahead this week with two upswings to hit all-time highs, leaving traders optimistic that the bull run could be sustained due to several positive factors.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka, which was the most-actively traded, jumped 150 kuna to 900 and pharmaceuticals group Pliva rose to 13,000 kuna from last Friday's 12,200 to lead the way.
Another popular issue, confectioner Kras, gained 80 kuna amid rumours that the EBRD was close to buying into the firm. But Kras denied rumours any kind of deal was imminent.
BUCHAREST
Bucharest shares traded mixed early in the week, drifting lower on Thursday amid thin investor interest.
Azomures SA fertiliser maker held centre stage, but closed the week 500 lei softer at 10,700.
The Bucharest stock exchange will not trade next week as it installs new software to improve trading and settlement.
LJUBLJANA

Slovenian shares started to recuperate slowly following the last week's slump to an all-time low as the market started to build optimism on the successful listing of a new issue of shares of drug maker Lek.

"The good performance of last week's listing of Lek's A issue brought optimism to the market and could fuel growth over the next week," one trader said. Since being listed on Wednesday last week, Lek's A shares have risen 18.1 percent.
The SBI index closed on Thursday at 928.72, up 3.0 points on the week.
